# North Pacific Strategy Initiative

> An independent research imprint publishing reference-grade working papers on Pacific sovereignty, bilateral financial architecture, and the defensive options available to middle powers in a period of dollar-system stress. Edited in Victoria, British Columbia. Working-paper text is licensed CC-BY-4.0; the imprint and wordmark are not licensed.

The site is plain static HTML and CSS. Every document page carries Highwire
citation_* meta tags and a Schema.org JSON-LD block (ScholarlyArticle,
TechArticle, Report, or PublicationIssue) for machine citation. Document IDs follow NPSI-WP-NNN for
working papers, NPSI-TB-NNN for technical briefings, NPSI-BN-NNN for briefing
notes, NPSI-SB-NNN for special briefings, and NPSI-PL-NNN for The Pacific
Ledger (the monthly Canada–Korea account). Special Briefings Nos. 4 and 5 keep
the date-based IDs printed on their releases (NPSI-20261003-B, NPSI-20261003-C):
these are accession numbers, assigned at intake; a publication serial is
assigned by the editor alone and is pending for both. The full register of
identifiers is https://npsi.ca/register/ (machine-readable: https://npsi.ca/registry.json).
Cite the canonical URLs below.

## Working Papers

- [WP11 — Rated AAA by the Issuer](https://npsi.ca/wp11/): What "open source" in AI has in common with a credit rating — the party applying the label is the party being labelled — and what documented base rates from four other unenforced quality labels (organic, Energy Star, "natural," credit ratings) say about how the vacuum resolves, forecast with probabilities and named falsifiers. Supersedes WP10 with a published correction notice. Technical Series; the current working paper. v1.0, 28 July 2026. PDF: https://npsi.ca/wp11/working-paper.pdf
- [WP9 — The Counterparty Problem](https://npsi.ca/wp9/): U.S. commitment reliability assessed as two separate questions — a documented record of roughly fifteen formal treaty exits since 2001, and a memorandum record for which no honest base rate exists. The 24 July 2026 PIF–EXIM $15 billion MoU priced against EXIM's 2015–2019 quorum lapse (financing down ~85%) and a charter expiring 31 December 2026. v1.0, 27 July 2026. PDF: https://npsi.ca/wp9/working-paper.pdf
- [WP10 — Fair Use for We, IP Theft for Thee](https://npsi.ca/wp10/): Nobody agrees what "open source" means in AI, and Washington is writing policy inside that vacuum — eleven model families read against the OSI definition (three qualify, none at frontier scale), the EU AI Act exemption, the litigation map, and the three legally distinct acts the debate keeps merging. Technical Series; every claim evidence-graded. Superseded by WP11 (corrections at its §1); remains available unaltered. v1.0, 26 July 2026. PDF (canonical): https://npsi.ca/wp10/working-paper.pdf
- [WP7 — Dazzle 2.0](https://npsi.ca/wp7/): Russia's "zebra" trucks and the contest between physical camouflage and machine vision — what the viral claim gets right, what it inflates, and the cost-asymmetry lesson for how NATO and Canada buy autonomy. First paper in the NPSI Counter-Autonomy series. v1.0, 12 July 2026. PDF: https://npsi.ca/wp7/working-paper.pdf
- [WP5 — Sovereign Compute North](https://npsi.ca/wp5/): An energy-for-memory swap, signed under Canadian law — a government-owned, allies-financed, Canadian-law-bound compute fabric anchored on surplus Canadian power and Korea-led sovereign capital, extended to the municipal layer. Co-issued with Fit For Gov; companion to SB1. v1.0, 27 May 2026. PDF: https://npsi.ca/wp5/working-paper.pdf
- [WP4 — The Addition Paradox](https://npsi.ca/wp4/): An energy thesis for Canada. The global energy transition added rather than substituted; chokepoint risk migrated from molecules to minerals; Canada uniquely holds the four assets the next forty years will reward. v1.0, 15 May 2026. PDF: https://npsi.ca/wp4/working-paper.pdf
- [WP3 — A Canada–Korea Pacific Defence-Industrial Corridor](https://npsi.ca/wp3/): Submarine procurement, industrial offsets, and the third rail of middle-power sovereignty. v1.0.1 (first published May 2026; revised 29 July 2026). PDF: https://npsi.ca/wp3/working-paper.pdf
- [WP2 — A Canada–United States Energy and Compute Compact](https://npsi.ca/wp2/): Canadian dispatchable generation paired with the U.S. grid; AI training on Canadian hydro, inference at the U.S. urban edge. v1.0, May 2026. PDF: https://npsi.ca/wp2/working-paper.pdf
- [WP1 — The Bilateral Foundation](https://npsi.ca/wp1/): A thirty-year Canada–Korea co-issued sovereign bond as the architecture of middle-power independence. v1.0, May 2026. PDF: https://npsi.ca/wp1/working-paper.pdf

## The Pacific Ledger

- [Issue index](https://npsi.ca/ledger/): The publication's home — current issue and archive.
- [№01 — July 2026 (Premier Issue)](https://npsi.ca/pl1/): A monthly account of the Canada–Korea relationship. Premier issue: Canada names TKMS preferred supplier over Hanwha's KSS-III on July 6 — and the relationship keeps posting entries anyway: LNG Canada's first cargo into KOGAS's Incheon terminal, Canadian crude to Korea planned to rise up to 3.3×, LG Energy Solution's agreed buyout of NextStar Windsor, a joint critical-minerals stockpiling plan due end-2026, fifty years of CANDU–KHNP, Defence Cooperation Agreement negotiations launched, and Kapyong at 75. NPSI-PL-001, issue closed 28 July 2026. PDF: https://npsi.ca/pl1/pacific-ledger.pdf

## Technical Briefings

- [TB1 — The Verified Sky](https://npsi.ca/tb1/): Sensing, certainty, and the law of automated airspace awareness — state of the art in computer vision and sensor fusion for monitoring defined airspace, the verification-ledger architecture, detection-to-action latency, lawful automated response in Canada, and a conservative capability forecast to 2031. v1.0, 11 June 2026. PDF: https://npsi.ca/tb1/technical-briefing.pdf

## Briefing Notes

- [BN1 — The Voter File](https://npsi.ca/bn1/): What every Canadian federal political party holds on every voter — the five-layer file — and the March 2026 statute (Bill C-4, Part 4) that placed it beyond every privacy law in the country, retroactive to 2000. v1.0, 11 June 2026. PDF: https://npsi.ca/bn1/briefing-note.pdf

## Special Briefings

- [SB5 — One Day, Four Names](https://npsi.ca/sb5/): What Tokyo, Seoul, Pyongyang and Washington each decided to call 15 August 1945, and the subject every name leaves out — six official names for one ending, each a sentence with a subject removed, read against the documents of 1945 (Stalin's message of 16 August accepting the order that split Korea, the refused line across Hokkaido, the three documents behind the 38th-parallel legend) and the speeches of 15 August 2026. ID NPSI-20261003-C. v1.0.1, 3 October 2026 (corrected 4 October). PDF (canonical, dark edition): https://npsi.ca/sb5/special-briefing.pdf · cream edition for print: https://npsi.ca/sb5/special-briefing-print.pdf
- [SB4 — The Tollgate Markets](https://npsi.ca/sb4/): Where breaking the rules costs a fee instead of a future — Turkey's 131 liquidated funds and 455,758 investors against a 2025 fine book of TRY 2.69 billion (about 1% of one fund), a seventeen-market ladder of enforcement in practice (the gain nobody measures, the fine nobody collects, the trial that never comes), and the Tollgate Test: five signs and four numbers to ask any regulator for. ID NPSI-20261003-B. v1.0.1, 3 October 2026 (corrected 4 October). PDF (canonical): https://npsi.ca/sb4/special-briefing.pdf
- [SB3 — The Ledger With One Entry](https://npsi.ca/sb3/): Venezuelan oil revenue under United States custody — an estimated $13 billion raised since January 2026 against one documented $300 million receipt and zero published audits; the two traps in American law (TRIA §201, Crystallex alter-ego doctrine) that made an offshore account the rational choice; and a benchmark against the three comparable oil-custody regimes, the most accountable of which still lost $8.8 billion. Accountability audit; every material claim confidence-rated. v1.0, 26 July 2026. PDF (canonical): https://npsi.ca/sb3/special-briefing.pdf
- [SB2 — The Three Doors](https://npsi.ca/sb2/): Under U.S. defense law, Canada has been a domestic source since 1992 (50 U.S.C. §4552) — a Canadian miner's map to American federal money via DPA Title III, Energy Act §18743, and EXIM's Supply Chain Resiliency Initiative. Ten-panel briefing. v1.0, 2 July 2026. PDF: https://npsi.ca/sb2/special-briefing.pdf
- [SB1 — Zero Secrets](https://npsi.ca/sb1/): Canada's data and AI sovereignty crisis — under the CLOUD Act and FISA 702, jurisdiction follows corporate ownership, not server location; an audit of the federal sovereign-AI agenda, four international models, and a three-stage response. Companion to WP5, Sovereign Compute North (https://npsi.ca/wp5/). v1.0, 11 June 2026. PDF: https://npsi.ca/sb1/special-briefing.pdf

## Indexes

- [Working Papers](https://npsi.ca/papers/): Every working paper by publication date — the current paper, the archive, and the numbering.
- [Briefings](https://npsi.ca/briefings/): Technical Briefings, Briefing Notes and Special Briefings, by publication date.
- [The Number Register](https://npsi.ca/register/): Every identifier the imprint has assigned — publication serials, accession numbers, and reserved numbers never released. Machine-readable form: https://npsi.ca/registry.json

## The Imprint

- [About](https://npsi.ca/about/): Mandate, methodology, and editorial standards.
- [Disclosure](https://npsi.ca/disclosure/): Declaration of interests — who writes and funds the imprint, every outside interest of the editor's that touches published subject matter, and which papers each interest touches.
- [Engage](https://npsi.ca/engage/): Contribution standards for named commentary, corrections, and technical critique.
- [Commentary](https://npsi.ca/commentary/): Named commentary index, per paper.
- [Colophon](https://npsi.ca/colophon/): Technical colophon — type, palette, infrastructure.

## Optional

- [Full index](https://npsi.ca/llms-full.txt): Complete abstracts, key findings, and citation metadata for every document, in one file.
- [Sitemap](https://npsi.ca/sitemap.xml)
- [Repository](https://github.com/cherishwins/npsi-site): Public version-controlled source for the site and papers.
